papers.title: Containment Problems in Convex Sets
papers.abstract: Let $P$ be a set of $n$ points in the plane, and let $C$ be a compact, convex subset of the plane that contains the origin in its interior. We study the problem of finding two points $p$ and $q$ of $P$ with the property that any homothet of $C$ that contains $p$ and $q$ must contain at least a constant fraction of the points of $P$. We give proofs for several cases. When $C$ is strictly convex we achieve a fraction of $1/5$, and when $C$ is a general convex region we achieve a fraction of $1/6e$. We show how the ideas of this second bound can be used to prove a lower bound for a version of the problem in $\mathbb{R}^d$ when $C$ is a $d$-ball. We also consider a few special cases. When $C$ is a triangle we get a lower bound of $1/12$, and when we allow that triangle to be rotated by $\pi$ radians in addition to being scaled and translated we get a lower bound of $1/768$. In proving this last result, we improve the state of the art on the version of this problem in three dimensions, where $C$ is a parallelepiped. We also consider the algorithmic aspects of finding such a pair of points.

papers.title: Reconfiguration of Time-Bounded Descriptions
papers.abstract: Time-bounded Kolmogorov complexity measures a string by the length of its shortest program that prints it within a deadline. An adjunction-universal machine (Bauwens, Kozachinskiy, and Shen, arXiv, 2025) is a Turing machine that simulates every Turing machine $M$ on every input $z$ with polynomial overhead when given a code of $M$, computable from $M$ in polynomial time, followed by $z$ unchanged. Any two adjunction-universal machines give the same measure up to an additive constant and a polynomial change of the deadline. However, this measure records only the shortest program for a string. We study all programs of one length that print a string within one deadline, join two of them when they differ in one bit, and ask when this graph is connected. Fix any adjunction-universal machine. For almost all $m$-bit strings and every deadline beyond some polynomial, the graph is disconnected at program length $m+O(1)$ and has at least $2^{m-O(1)}$ components at length $2m+3$. In contrast, we build an adjunction-universal machine in which every such graph is connected or empty, at every deadline, once the program length reaches a computable threshold that is at most exponential in the length of the string. Exponential thresholds are unavoidable: for every adjunction-universal machine with such thresholds and every large $m$, more than three quarters of the $m$-bit strings need a threshold exponential in $m$. For our machine, above the threshold, every program for the string is within three bit flips of a connected set of fastest programs for the string, along a path inside the graph, at every deadline by which that program halts. For this machine, deciding whether two given programs are connected in this graph is $\mathsf{PSPACE}$-complete when the input is the string, the deadline in unary and the two programs; for each fixed string it takes polynomial time.

papers.title: What remains of the planar induced minor conjectures?
papers.abstract: Dallard, Milani\v{c}, and \v{S}torgel, and independently Gartland and Lokshtanov, conjectured that for every planar graph $H$, Maximum Weight Independent Set and List $3$-Coloring are polynomial-time solvable in $H$-induced-minor-free graphs. As a structural explanation, Gartland and Lokshtanov further conjectured that such graphs admit balanced separators dominated by a constant number of vertices. Bonnet and Chang recently refuted the independent-set part of the algorithmic conjecture, by showing that Maximum Independent Set is $\mathsf{NP}$-hard in graphs excluding the $5\times5$ grid as an induced minor. We revisit both conjectures. We show that the graphs used by Bonnet and Chang exclude much simpler planar graphs, including several $16$-vertex trees, and we introduce a second, independent family of hard instances. We also prove that $3$-Coloring is $\mathsf{NP}$-hard in both settings, thus refuting the algorithmic conjecture in full, even in its quasipolynomial version, unless $\mathsf{NP}\subseteq\mathsf{QP}$. On the structural side, we identify planar graphs $H$ for which the structural conjecture holds, while the algorithmic one fails. Thus, constantly dominated balanced separators cannot by themselves explain the tractability of Maximum Weight Independent Set and List $3$-Coloring.

papers.title: Proper Conflict-Free Coloring of Undirected Path, Chordal Bipartite, and Strongly Chordal Graphs
papers.abstract: A proper conflict-free coloring is a proper coloring in which each nonisolated vertex has a neighbor whose color occurs exactly once in its open neighborhood. We prove that deciding whether the clique number of colors suffices is NP-complete on undirected path graphs, even with a supplied representation by paths in a star. One extra color suffices on every instance in the reduction. We also prove NP-completeness on chordal bipartite graphs for every fixed palette size $k\ge4$. For strongly chordal graphs, reverse simple elimination gives a constructive upper bound of one more than the clique number. We obtain exact polynomial-time algorithms under several conditions on the maximum cliques, including when they induce a connected subtree of a clique tree. For strictly chordal graphs we characterize the optimum and construct an optimal coloring in $O(n+m)$ time, where $n$ and $m$ count the vertices and edges. For strongly chordal graphs with clique-tree separators of size at most $s$, we give an exact algorithm in $n^{2^{O(s+1)}}$ time, with no bound on the clique number.

papers.title: Vertex Deletion on $H$-Induced-Minor-Free Graphs: Subexponential FPT Algorithms and Approximation Schemes
papers.abstract: We study vertex-deletion problems on string graphs and, more generally, on graphs excluding a fixed graph as an induced minor. For every fixed graph $H$, fixed nonnegative integer $t$, and fixed monadic second-order formula $\phi$, we consider the problem of finding a minimum-cardinality set $S$ such that $G-S$ has treewidth at most $t$ and satisfies $\phi$. This captures classic problems such as Vertex Cover, Feedback Vertex Set, and deletion to graphs of any fixed bounded treewidth. We give an algorithm with running time $2^{k^{2/3} \log^{O(1)} k}n^{O(1)}$ on $H$-induced-minor-free graphs, where $k$ is the optimum deletion-set size. This resolves in the affirmative the open problem highlighted by Bonnet and Rz\k{a}\.{z}ewski [Algorithmica 2019] and Berthe, Bougeret, Gon\c{c}alves, and Raymond [ICALP 2025] regarding the existence of a subexponential parameterized algorithm for Feedback Vertex Set on string graphs. Our algorithm significantly improves over existing parameterized algorithms for more restricted classes of problems on more restricted classes of graphs. When the property defined by $\phi$ is hereditary, we also obtain a quasi-polynomial time approximation scheme, namely an algorithm that produces a $(1+\varepsilon)$-approximate solution in quasi-polynomial time. Both the sub-exponential algorithm and the quasi-polynomial time approximation scheme build on the same new structural and algorithmic insights.

papers.title: Pangenome Peeling: Decomposing Weighted Adjacencies into Path-Forest Genomes
papers.abstract: One aspect of pangenome analysis that has received little attention is the recovery of the individual genomes that gave rise to a pangenome graph. While substantial effort has focused on constructing pangenomes from collections of genomes, the inverse problem remains largely unexplored: given a pangenome represented as a set of weighted adjacencies, can we reconstruct the constituent linear genomes that underlie it? Thus we introduce the pangenome peeling problem, which seeks to decompose a weighted adjacency graph into a collection of linear genomes whose combined adjacencies reproduce the observed edge weights. This problem is particularly relevant when considering ancestral pangenomes, where the graph structure may be known or inferred, but the underlying genomes are not. As a first step toward addressing this problem, we formally define pangenome peeling and derive a lower bound on the minimum number of genomes required to explain a given weighted adjacency graph. We then present two reconstruction methods: one based on the sequential addition of edges and a second based on extracting maximum-spanning-tree structures. Both methods produce genome collections that exactly explain the input adjacency data. To evaluate the recovered sets of genomes, we compare them to the set of input genomes using a maximum-weight matching framework based on the double-cut-and-join distance with indels. Here the maximum-spanning tree approach is superior, producing sets of constituent genomes close to the simulations while the sequential addition of edges approach yields constituent genomes increasingly divergent from the input as genomes sizes increase.

papers.title: Matroid products via submodular coupling
papers.abstract: The study of matroid products traces back to the 1970s, when Lov\'asz and Mason studied the existence of various types of matroid products with different strengths. Among these, the tensor product is arguably the most important, which can be considered as an extension of the tensor product from linear algebra. However, Las Vergnas showed that the tensor product of two matroids does not always exist. Over the following four decades, matroid products remained surprisingly underexplored, regaining attention only in recent years due to applications in tropical geometry and the limit theory of matroids. In this paper, inspired by the concept of coupling in probability theory, we introduce the notion of coupling for matroids -- or, more generally, for submodular set functions. This operation can be viewed as a relaxation of the tensor product. Unlike the tensor product, however, we prove that a coupling always exists for any two submodular functions and can be chosen to be increasing if the original functions are increasing. As a corollary, we show that two matroids always admit a matroid coupling, leading to a novel operation on matroids. Our construction is algorithmic, providing an oracle for the coupling matroid through a polynomial number of oracle calls to the original matroids. We apply this construction to derive new necessary conditions for matroid representability and establish connection between tensor products and Ingleton's inequality. Additionally, we verify the existence of set functions that are universal with respect to a given property, meaning any set function over a finite domain with that property can be obtained as a quotient.

papers.title: On Multi-label radio Labelings of Graphs
papers.abstract: We propose and study a multi-labeling generalization of the $k$-radio labeling problem of graphs: given a graph $G$ and integers $k$ and $m$, assign to each vertex of $G$ a set of $m$ integer labels such that distinct labels assigned to a vertex differ by at least $k+1$, and the labels of any two distinct vertices $x$ and $y$ pairwise differ by at least $k+1-d(x,y)$, with $d(x,y)$ being the distance between vertices $x$ and $y$. We prove general bounds on the minimum span of such a labeling and more refined results for the case $k=1$. For paths and cycles, we derive sharp bounds on the minimum span when $k$ is small. We finally propose a conjecture for the minimum span on the path and for an almost-tight bound on the cycle.

papers.title: Bounded Relative Boundary Implies Narrow DNF Approximation
papers.abstract: We prove Friedgut's conjecture (J. Amer. Math. Soc. 12 (1999)) that every increasing family in the $p$-biased discrete cube with bounded relative boundary can be approximated arbitrarily well by one whose minimal elements have size bounded independently of the dimension and the bias. For $0<p\le 1/2$, every increasing Boolean function with total resampling influence at most $K$ is $\varepsilon$-close under $\mu_p^n$ to a monotone DNF of width $\exp(O((K+1)^2/\varepsilon^2))$, from which the full conjecture follows for all $p\in(0,1)$. We build on Hatami's pseudo-junta theorem (Ann. of Math. 176 (2012)), whose approximator need not be increasing. Our randomized shifts produce an increasing approximator that is measurable with respect to a controlled refinement of Hatami's adaptive partition. Retaining only short positive certificates yields the desired narrow DNF.

papers.title: Effective Horizons for Prophet Inequalities with Discounted I.I.D. Rewards
papers.abstract: We study prophet inequalities for $n$ i.i.d. base rewards subject to multiplicative discounts across $S$ phases. For equal-length phases and a common discount factor $\widetilde\gamma$, we characterize the optimal competitive ratio of single-quantile policies as $n\to\infty$ with $S$ and $\widetilde\gamma$ fixed. The resulting sharp guarantee describes the dependence on the phase parameters: it recovers $1-1/e$ without discounting and approaches $1/2$ in the worst-case regime. We also establish a distribution-free comparison that bounds the discounted prophet by a fractional i.i.d. maximum with effective horizon $B$, the sum of the discount weights across all observations. The comparison yields acceptance probability $1/B$, determined only by the phase profile. This calibration attains the canonical optimum even among single-quantile policies that may choose their acceptance probability using the known base distribution. The comparison also gives guarantees for heterogeneous discounts and unequal phase lengths. A complementary optimal-stopping upper bound establishes the same limiting optimum of $1/2$ for arbitrary stopping rules in the canonical model. Finally, the same effective-horizon calibration sets acceptance probability $1-\widetilde\gamma$ under infinite-horizon geometric discounting. This explicit quantile rule attains Boshuizen's (1994) known optimal worst-case ratio $1/(1+\widetilde\gamma)$ without solving a Bellman equation.
